trust_decision.summary: Whether an HTTP request's Host header names a host the server is meant to serve (DNS-rebinding defence). At the pinned commit nothing decides it; the fix adds one root-router middleware that compares r.Host exactly against the --allowed-hosts set (default '*').

landing_point.why: The existing CORS block is the only origin-related code, and its warning already mentions DNS rebinding (server.go:377), so a reader of an 'origin validation' summary goes here first.

fix_sites.entry_point: every HTTP route on the root chi router (/, /api/*, /mcp/*, /ui/*), all served by the one http.Server at server.go:359
ServerConfig struct consumed by server.NewServer (public Go API, internal package)
CLI flag --allowed-hosts on the toolbox command

O3_reason_to_dismiss: There is little to dismiss: one root middleware covers every route. The only arguable leave-alone is stdio mode (server.go:439-442), which has no Host header at all.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The default wildcard must still accept any Host (the fix keeps '*' as the default), and the SSE endpoint event builds the client's message URL from r.Host. A strict default allow-list, or one that drops the port, breaks existing deployments and SSE clients reached by a non-local hostname.

O6_input_shapes: exact Host header string including port (e.g. 'localhost:5000'), map lookup with no case, port or trailing-dot normalisation

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Have the SSE endpoint event's message URL take its host from X-Forwarded-Host (falling back to r.Host). The Host check validates one header while the URL handed to the client comes from another.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The handler already trusts X-Forwarded-Proto two lines above (mcp.go:292), so a maintainer adding proxy support would plausibly read X-Forwarded-Host the same way.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second http.Server, such as a UI or health listener on its own port, built with its own chi router that does not get the root middleware.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The --ui flag already mounts a separate router (web.go:19-33); splitting it onto its own listener is a plausible refactor, and the copied router would miss the check.

O9_family: CWE-346 origin validation / DNS rebinding (missing Host header allow-list)

O10_build.project_tests: internal/server/server_test.go (TestServe starts the server on 127.0.0.1:5000), internal/server/mcp_test.go (CORS header checks around line 1042), cmd/root_test.go TestServerConfigFlags; these need no database

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Tighten --allowed-origins / CORS (or default it to localhost) instead of adding a Host-header check, which leaves non-browser rebinding requests open.

out_of_scope_notes: internal/server/mcp.go:255: the SSE handler hard-codes Access-Control-Allow-Origin '*', overriding the configured --allowed-origins CORS policy. This is the CORS protection, not the Host check, and the fix leaves it unchanged.
